decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: draft covers “saving”; Round 1 client: “I can save a link.”
decisions.note: Specification-stage decision supports saving a bookmark from a link and is consistent with the reference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: draft covers “tagging”; Round 1 client: “organize things with tags.”
decisions.note: Specification-stage tagging decision conforms; no incompatible tag behavior was presented.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: draft covers “searching”; Round 1 client: “search for them.”
decisions.note: The recorded high-level search decision is consistent with the reference. Unmentioned advanced search details are not treated as presented departures.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: draft covers “editing”; Round 1 client explicitly approves editing.
decisions.note: The presented editing capability is reference-consistent; the summary does not present an incompatible restriction on editable fields.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: draft covers “deleting bookmarks”; Round 1 client approves deleting and a confirmation first.
decisions.note: Specification-stage delete capability conforms. Confirmation is an orthogonal safeguard.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker separately presents “archiving, restoring, and deleting”; Round 1 client approves “archive or delete.”
decisions.note: Separate reversible archiving/restoration and deletion are consistent with the archive-versus-delete requirements.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client describes the presented specification as “warning me instead of making a duplicate” and approves it.
decisions.note: At the specification review, the recorded duplicate behavior prevents duplication and is reference-conforming.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client asks to ensure a pasted link fills its title automatically; Round 2 maker resolves this: “pasting a valid link starts retrieval automatically”; Round 2 client confirms it is “exactly what I asked about.”
decisions.note: Linked specification clarification and plan disposition form one decision. Automatic title collection conforms; the record does not explicitly decide against collecting the other metadata, so their omission from the summary is not classified as divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: the retrieved title “remains editable” and “never overwrites a title the user types”; Round 2 client explicitly approves both behaviors.
decisions.note: Plan-stage title editing behavior conforms to editing auto-collected metadata.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker presents tasks for “saving and automatic title retrieval”; Round 3 client approves “saving with the automatic title.”
decisions.note: Task-artifact review reiterates the conforming automatic-title behavior without presenting an incompatible metadata rule.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: “Automatic title suggestions immediately after pasting or leaving a URL”; Round 4 client verifies that “Example Domain” was filled automatically.
decisions.note: Implementation-review decision conforms for automatic title collection. No exclusive title-only rule is stated, so absent metadata claims are not inferred as divergence.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: “Editable titles with protection against overwriting manual input”; Round 4 client reports the important behaviors work.
Round 4 maker presents “Newest-first browsing”; Round 2 client had approved “browsing newest-first.”
decisions.note: Newest-first is a date-added sort order consistent with the reference. The presentation does not explicitly prohibit other sort keys, so no divergence is inferred.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker presents “tags” and “combined filters”; Round 4 client verifies saving with tags, while Round 2 client had approved filtering by tags.
decisions.note: Implementation-stage tag assignment and tag filtering are reference-consistent.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker presents “Duplicate-link warnings with explicit continuation.” Round 4 client says the attempt “warns me and points to the one I already have” and broadly approves, but never mentions or accepts the ability to continue creating a duplicate.
decisions.note: Implementation review introduces a departure: permitting explicit continuation after a duplicate warning does not ensure that re-saving converges to editing the existing bookmark. The client neither corrects this nor explicitly identifies and accepts the save-anyway difference; broad approval is insufficient.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: “Editing, archiving, restoring, and confirmed permanent deletion”; Round 4 client verifies archive, restore, and permanent delete.
decisions.note: Implementation-stage archive and permanent-delete behavior maintains the required reversible-versus-permanent distinction.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 app presentation is followed by the client’s direct verification: “find it in the archived view, restore it.”
decisions.note: The reviewed implementation provides a separate archived view, conforming to the reference.
